news_analysis.headline_hook: Rs 4,00,000 Crore Vanished: The Math of Your Portfolio Decay.
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty fell over 1% in a single session, eroding roughly Rs 4 lakh crore in total market capitalization as sensational headline triggers sparked retail panic.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors assume 'Rs 4 Lakh Crore wiped out' means actual cash vanished from the financial system, prompting panic selling to salvage capital from what media portrays as an impending structural market collapse.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: Institutions leverage sensational media narrative headlines to trigger retail stop-loss cascades, absorbing quality liquidity at lower valuations while total market cap paper losses simply reflect routine mark-to-market fluctuations.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Ignore cumulative market-cap loss headlines; never panic-sell fundamentally sound holdings based on single-day 1% index drawdowns.

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: 'Rs 4 Lakh Crore wiped out means cash physically left the financial system and the market is structurally collapsing.'
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: Over 1% index drawdowns represent routine mark-to-market repricing of marginal valuations, not liquidated cash.

stat_data.label: benchmark index drawdown in a single session
stat_data.context: A 1% drop across Sensex and Nifty triggers algorithmic stop-loss cascades. Media houses weaponize Rs 4 Lakh Crore paper-loss figures to induce maximum retail panic.

flowchart_data.title: Stop-Loss Cascades
flowchart_data.description: Retail algorithmic and manual stop losses fire simultaneously at key support levels.

flowchart_data.title: Institutional Accumulation
flowchart_data.description: Institutional desks step in to quietly absorb high-quality liquidity at discounted valuations.

slides.headline:
The Hidden Cost
Of Panic Selling
slides.card_text: Selling fundamentally sound assets during a 1% headline-driven index drawdown locks in permanent capital destruction. You convert temporary paper fluctuations into realized losses, transferring your equity directly to institutional balance sheets at distressed prices.

slides.headline:
The Non-Negotiable
Execution Rule
slides.card_text: Ignore cumulative market-cap loss headlines completely. Never panic-sell fundamentally sound holdings based on single-day index percentage drops. True risk management relies on asset-specific structural integrity, not aggregate media panic figures.
